sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree by enrollment, no master’s required; strong proof-based advanced calculus, abstract/linear
algebra and advanced electives expected. Department says mathematics grades should mostly be A/A−.
UChicago math bachelor meets degree-route eligibility if completed before entry; F-1 does not itself disqualify.
This is not an admissions-likelihood assessment. [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through SAS Slate to Mathematics PhD (AMCS is separate). Gather CV, academic/personal statement,
unofficial transcripts and 3-5 referees; investigate English waiver and fee waiver early. Only one program
application within the same Penn school is allowed. No prearranged supervisor required. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Committee makes admissions decisions. Contact at most one or two professors for substantive research-fit
discussion; no mass emails or requests for individual admission. Mention faculty in statement. Current
directory identifies Angela Gibney as Graduate Chair; some older personal pages still call Donagi chair. General
inquiries: graduate@math.upenn.edu. [s1] [s7]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application cannot be edited after submission. Required documents should be correct first; email
necessary additions to math administrator. Receipt/status available afterward; decision letter appears in portal
with automated email. Only one application per school. No portal account or referee invitation was created
during this research. [s1] [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Explicit 2027 admissions pages verified directly. Department has partially updated pages containing December
7/8/15 conflicts and 2025-26/2026-27 stipend rows; distinguish dated statements. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
Authoritative explicit Fall 2027 deadline: 8 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern/EST, agreed by central SAS
calendar and math FAQ. However, How to Apply retains a parenthetical saying submit by December 7, and
program description retains December 15 in an older paragraph. Clarify with graduate@math.upenn.edu;
prudent planning target is December 7, not a newly asserted official deadline. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]
Funding consideration [Unresolved]
Standard five-year funding accompanies PhD admission; no separate initial math funding application/deadline
found. Use the current admission deadline and verify any Bridge fellowship supplement or outside-award
deadline independently. [s3] [s10]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Aim for 8 December 2026. Math allows letters a few days later, but no exact guaranteed grace cutoff is given.
Another paragraph says after December 15 is possible and old text mentions end-December/mid-January;
these stale provisions should not be used as a reliable 2027 deadline. After January 1, notify the Graduate
Group Chair of additions. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Required scores should be received for timely review; math permits scores a few days after application
deadline without an exact guaranteed grace cutoff. GRE optional; English exemption likely for complete
four-year UChicago study. ETS code 2926; allow reporting time rather than relying on stale mid-January
language. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Required applicant documents accompany the application by 8 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST. The school
cannot review an application that was not submitted. Later supplementary documents may be emailed to the
math administrator; additions after January 1 require a follow-up to the Graduate Group Chair. No guaranteed
later document deadline. [s1] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Department explicitly gives April 15 as the PhD offer acceptance deadline and says offers expire then. Treat as
a standing Penn policy and verify the dated 2027 offer. Its claim that every US program shares this rule is
overbroad; see shared CGS qualifications. [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL or IELTS unless exempt. Department looks for TOEFL total at least 100 and speaking at least 20 on the
older scale; IELTS minimum 7. Current public page does not translate these numbers to the 2026 TOEFL scale.
English scores valid two years. Non-native PhDs must establish spoken-English teaching proficiency before
second year; department mentions TOEFL speaking 27 or its internal test. [s2] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Entire four-year undergraduate study in the US qualifies under the math rule; confirm if transfer/study history
differs. Central SAS asks applicants to contact their program about waiver activation, generally after uploading
unofficial transcript. Admission exemption does not automatically waive later teaching-language certification;
summer International TA preparation may require early arrival and carries additional stipend. [s3] [s4] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; How to Apply broadly welcomes GRE scores if available. No explicit not-considered prohibition.
Confirm current portal if submitting General GRE, because FAQ specifically discusses Mathematics only. [s1]

GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional, accepted and used as an information point in review. Earlier-year valid scores permitted; GRE validity
five years. ETS institution 2926, mathematics department 0703. [s2] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three, at most five. Prefer mathematics professors who can assess proof-based coursework, projects,
research ability and mathematical engagement. Names of at least three must be entered before submission.
[s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional standard-funding reference requirement found. Bridge fellowship application/reference questions
and international eligibility are not established by the transition notice; old discontinued Bridge master’s rules
do not safely establish new fellowship rules. [s3] [s10]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Math program description explicitly describes letters being uploaded once the applicant submits with
recommender names. It does not clearly state whether merely entering names sends invitations immediately.
Public central FAQ does not resolve timing; ask admissions before relying on pre-submission invitations. [s3] [s5]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Letters need not be received before application submission. Whether invitations are exclusively
post-submission is not conclusively established; the math description uses that workflow. [s3] [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
After submission, Slate shows status and receipt of supporting documentation. Applicant should continue
monitoring until complete. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
After submitting, additional unlisted referees cannot upload directly; ask them to email Reshma Tanna with
identification and request that the letter be added to the Math graduate application. Submitted-letter
replacement, cross-cycle reuse and Mathematics Interfolio handling are not publicly established. Do not import
another Penn department’s Interfolio policy. [s1]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required CV/resume upload. Public math checklist gives no specific content prompt, length limit, font/margin
or file-format rule; inspect current upload field. [s1]

Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required statement, called Personal Statement in math instructions and Statement of Purpose centrally.
Prompt paraphrase: explain how background and academic experience led to graduate study and Penn;
research interests, intellectual goals, educational trajectory, curiosity and ambitions. Math additionally
recommends concrete mathematical problems/theories, how interest developed, new work/results and future
vision, and Penn faculty of interest. Length, spacing, font, file type and upload/link specification beyond an
application statement are not publicly fixed; do not copy another department’s two-page rule. [s1] [s4]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Part of the required combined statement: prompt paraphrase asks how personal experience and perspective
could enrich Penn’s learning community. No separate background essay is listed. Separate length/format
remains unverified. [s1]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
In the combined statement, include specific mathematical problems/theories and faculty fit. No separate
research-interest statement listed; distinct prompt/limit unverified. [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list [Unresolved]
Not listed as a separate required mathematics document in reviewed checklists. Public instructions do not
establish whether an optional research proposal, thesis/sample or publication attachment/link is accepted;
confirm portal. Publications/research can be discussed in CV/statement, without implying full-paper submission
permission. [s1] [s2] [s4]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
Not separately listed in mathematics/central public checklists; transcript required. No public course-list or
course-description prompt, length, formatting or upload/link requirement established. Verify Mathematics
supplement rather than assuming optional attachments are permitted. [s1] [s4]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate initial standard-support essay found. Bridge has transitioned to a PhD fellowship; the public
transition notice does not provide current prompts, word limits, formatting, submission route or reference
questions. Ask the math office if seeking that fellowship. [s3] [s10]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
AI policy permits limited brainstorming, organization, grammar/style, citation and language assistance on
applicant-owned ideas. Substantial AI-generated application content presented as one’s own, unverifiable
claims, and AI during interviews/assessments without express authorization are prohibited. Applicant must be
able to explain and substantiate submissions. No additional Mathematics essay publicly identified. [s6]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
Math explicitly lists USD 49,000 for a 12-month 2026-27 fellowship plus tuition, fees and health insurance.
Older FAQ’s USD 43,050 is labeled 2025-26. Ratified CBA Article 5 raises the covered-worker annual minimum
by 3% on 1 July 2027: calculated USD 50,470 (also stated in union summary). However, educational fellows
without teaching/research services are excluded from the bargaining unit; therefore USD 50,470 is a
covered-worker minimum, not yet a verified first-year math fellowship offer for 2027-28. [s3] [s2] [s8] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five years for full-time PhDs making timely progress. At least two academic years (including first) and three
summers have no teaching; at least two academic years of teaching required. Sixth year needs prior approval
and is not guaranteed funded; older FAQ says tuition/fees become applicant responsibility, with possible
modest TA stipend. Verify actual offer and CBA application. [s2] [s11]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department’s PhD support promise is not citizenship-limited: inference that admitted F-1 students qualify. CBA

also expressly provides international-worker protections/funding. Specific outside awards or Bridge fellowship
may have separate nationality restrictions, presently unverified. [s3] [s9] [s10]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Good standing and timely progress; TA training and teaching-English certification where applicable.
Department describes TA duties up to 12 hours/week and optional additional paid summer teaching.
Covered-worker internship pay can offset stipend under CBA. Confirm appointment duties/pay schedule and
union deductions in offer. [s3] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate initial standard five-year-support application identified. Faculty research-grant fellowships and
Bridge fellowship consideration may require additional departmental process; current Bridge details not public
on reviewed pages. [s3] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Faculty grants can provide additional teaching-free periods; optional summer teaching can earn additional
stipend. Bridge fellowship opportunity exists following closure of Bridge master’s admissions. External
fellowships need separate eligibility checks. [s3] [s10]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 90; credit/debit card at submission, international instructions specify major credit card. Central FAQ also
mentions a nonrefundable enrollment fee after accepting, but does not establish a Mathematics amount or
whether exempted for funded PhDs. [s2] [s4] [s5]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Limited financial-hardship waivers for PhD applicants, administered centrally; no citizenship restriction stated
on reviewed current form guidance. Begin application, select request or supplied waiver-code option; FINALIZE
application before review. Submit at least two weeks before deadline (calculated 24 November 2026 for Dec
8); reviews take 7-14 business days. Do not pay while awaiting decision even if paywall appears; no refund.
Denial requires payment. Use portal form, not emailed financial details; no status inquiry until 14 business
days. [s4] [s3]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree by enrollment, no master’s required; strong proof-based advanced calculus, abstract/linear
algebra and advanced electives expected. Department says mathematics grades should mostly be A/A−.
UChicago math bachelor meets degree-route eligibility if completed before entry; F-1 does not itself disqualify.
This is not an admissions-likelihood assessment. [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through SAS Slate to Mathematics PhD (AMCS is separate). Gather CV, academic/personal statement,
unofficial transcripts and 3-5 referees; investigate English waiver and fee waiver early. Only one program
application within the same Penn school is allowed. No prearranged supervisor required. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Committee makes admissions decisions. Contact at most one or two professors for substantive research-fit
discussion; no mass emails or requests for individual admission. Mention faculty in statement. Current
directory identifies Angela Gibney as Graduate Chair; some older personal pages still call Donagi chair. General
inquiries: graduate@math.upenn.edu. [s1] [s7]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application cannot be edited after submission. Required documents should be correct first; email
necessary additions to math administrator. Receipt/status available afterward; decision letter appears in portal
with automated email. Only one application per school. No portal account or referee invitation was created
during this research. [s1] [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Explicit 2027 admissions pages verified directly. Department has partially updated pages containing December
7/8/15 conflicts and 2025-26/2026-27 stipend rows; distinguish dated statements. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]

Academic application [Conflict]
Authoritative explicit Fall 2027 deadline: 8 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern/EST, agreed by central SAS
calendar and math FAQ. However, How to Apply retains a parenthetical saying submit by December 7, and
program description retains December 15 in an older paragraph. Clarify with graduate@math.upenn.edu;

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
Standard five-year funding accompanies PhD admission; no separate initial math funding application/deadline
found. Use the current admission deadline and verify any Bridge fellowship supplement or outside-award
deadline independently. [s3] [s10]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Aim for 8 December 2026. Math allows letters a few days later, but no exact guaranteed grace cutoff is given.
Another paragraph says after December 15 is possible and old text mentions end-December/mid-January;
these stale provisions should not be used as a reliable 2027 deadline. After January 1, notify the Graduate
Group Chair of additions. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Required scores should be received for timely review; math permits scores a few days after application
deadline without an exact guaranteed grace cutoff. GRE optional; English exemption likely for complete
four-year UChicago study. ETS code 2926; allow reporting time rather than relying on stale mid-January
language. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Required applicant documents accompany the application by 8 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST. The school
cannot review an application that was not submitted. Later supplementary documents may be emailed to the
math administrator; additions after January 1 require a follow-up to the Graduate Group Chair. No guaranteed
later document deadline. [s1] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Department explicitly gives April 15 as the PhD offer acceptance deadline and says offers expire then. Treat as
a standing Penn policy and verify the dated 2027 offer. Its claim that every US program shares this rule is
overbroad; see shared CGS qualifications. [s2]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL or IELTS unless exempt. Department looks for TOEFL total at least 100 and speaking at least 20 on the
older scale; IELTS minimum 7. Current public page does not translate these numbers to the 2026 TOEFL scale.
English scores valid two years. Non-native PhDs must establish spoken-English teaching proficiency before
second year; department mentions TOEFL speaking 27 or its internal test. [s2] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Entire four-year undergraduate study in the US qualifies under the math rule; confirm if transfer/study history
differs. Central SAS asks applicants to contact their program about waiver activation, generally after uploading
unofficial transcript. Admission exemption does not automatically waive later teaching-language certification;
summer International TA preparation may require early arrival and carries additional stipend. [s3] [s4] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; How to Apply broadly welcomes GRE scores if available. No explicit not-considered prohibition.
Confirm current portal if submitting General GRE, because FAQ specifically discusses Mathematics only. [s1]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial academic transcripts with application. Official final records, including degree conferral and all
previous academic work, required after accepting admission; must come directly from institution/electronic
service to sas-gradadmissions@sas.upenn.edu, not from applicant or undergraduate admissions office. No

At least three, at most five. Prefer mathematics professors who can assess proof-based coursework, projects,

and is not guaranteed funded; older FAQ says tuition/fees become applicant responsibility, with possible
modest TA stipend. Verify actual offer and CBA application. [s2] [s11]
